summary: Round 4, confirming, scoped to the one-word revert. VERIFIED MECHANICALLY, not by reading: I extracted the diff embedded in the round-3 packet and it hashes to exactly 57ddc63d, the round-3 approved bytes, so the two are directly comparable. diff of the two diffs yields precisely two lines: the backlog.md blob index (ba76932..dbc2419 -> ba76932..1b053b0, a necessary consequence of the content change) and the M3.5 backlog row, differing in the single token '~166 files' -> '~152 files'. Nothing else. Hunk-level sha256 confirms it independently: the MemoryFlatAtIntervalCeilingTest.java hunk is 63faed2b in BOTH rounds and the http/build.gradle.kts hunk is f78756b7 in BOTH, byte-identical. The round-3 sampler hardening is intact in the staged bytes -- the 3x retry with samplerFailures.add at attempt==2 (line 240), the catch(Throwable) around the sampler loop (line 260), the assertThat(samplerFailures).isEmpty() (line 322) and the last-sample-within-5s timestamp assertion (line 327) are all present and unmoved. No test code, no Gradle, no other prose changed; no assertion added, removed, or weakened. Per instruction I did not re-run the 3.5-minute test and did not re-open the design, the 2.0 threshold, the hardening or the process decisions. On the second question: ~152 is the correct figure for what that sentence claims, and MY OWN ROUND-3 MINOR WAS WRONG ABOUT WHICH DOCUMENT WAS STALE. I measured 166 regular files in the whole store root and asserted the comment was the stale copy; the sentence in fact claims the LOAD's flush count, which is a different quantity. Re-derived from the test's own fixture rather than taken on trust: the record is a ~41-byte action line plus a 189-byte doc (180-char pad), 231 bytes; a blocking 1000-record chunk is ~226 KiB, matching the '~223 KB' the prose carries; 24 concurrent producers contribute one chunk each per flush, so ~5.54 MB per flush; 200 MiB / 5.54 MB is ~37.8 flushes, x4 files per flush = ~151 load files, and adding the three sendTinyBulk flushes (2 warm-up + 1 probe, 12 files) plus the 2 index-registry objects gives ~165 store-root total. That reproduces BOTH measurements to within one file of rounding on the tail chunk: 152 for the load, 166 for the root. The two numbers are real measurements of different quantities exactly as the author states, the revert restores the one the sentence is about, and the commit no longer contradicts itself between backlog.md:196 and the test comment at line 349, which is what round 3 asked for. Worth stating for the record: the figure is prose only. It appears in a comment and a backlog row and no assertion depends on it -- the cadence check asserts files/s < 2.0 over deltas of the absolute count, which is warm-up-independent, and the sample-count guard is hasSizeGreaterThan(10). So neither value could ever change whether this test catches a bug; what was at stake was a self-contradicting commit, and that is now resolved. No blocking or major findings. The two remaining round-3 minors (the uncounted files-per-flush invariant, and the 175 MB of scratch never deleted) are untouched by this delta and stay recorded for the milestone boundary per rule 13 -- not to be opened as a further round.
